content.text: Intent
A register of the legal entities FCY does business with — the house term "counterparty" (per the FCY glossary, the
entity
, not CDM's role-on-a-trade meaning). Every counterparty is identified as a CDM
Party

with an LEI per FCY standing rule R7, and no free-text counterparty names appear anywhere else in the system: this register is where those names and identifiers live. It serves trade booking, the governing-agreement stack (each ISDA Master, CSA, GMRA or GMSLA is signed with one entity here) and regulatory counterparty classification. Population is ~40 active institutional counterparties, all UK or EEA.
Scope
IN: one LegalEntity register — names, LEI, EMIR category, business segment, lifecycle (draft / active / retired).
IN: LEI uniqueness and format; retirement excludes an entity from new business while preserving its history.
OUT: agent/fund/umbrella structures (which fund trades under which manager) — separate spec if wanted.
OUT: the master-agreement stack (ISDA, CSA, GMRA, GMSLA) — separate spec; this register only supplies the entity each agreement is signed with.
OUT: trade booking, margin, reporting flows that
consume
this register.
Scenarios
None — the bean's standard screens: create, edit, browse, retire. No cross-record process beyond the uniqueness and retirement rules, which the requirements and the table carry.
Requirements
R1: retired — carried by the table rule unique-when-present on LegalEntity.lei; an LEI is globally unique to one entity (ISO 17442), so a retired entity's LEI is never re-used.

R2: WHEN a legal entity is retired, the system SHALL exclude it from the register's selection surface — the counterparty picker this register provides to every consuming flow — while keeping the record and all references to it intact. (Trade booking and the agreement stack honour this exclusion; they are specified elsewhere.)
P1: retired — carried by the table rule unique-when-present on LegalEntity.lei.
P2: retired — carried by the table rule format(20 alphanumeric) on LegalEntity.lei.
P3: a retired legal entity is immutable except for its status and retirement date.
P4: retirement is one-way — status SHALL NOT move from retired back to draft or active; facing the entity again means a new register entry.
Data model
bean: LegalEntity

cells.text: the legal name as it appears on the governing agreement
the counterparty-population segment from the counterparties page; default(INTERDEALER_OTHER)
all current counterparties are UK or EEA

content.text: Realises CDM
cyai.cdm.base.staticdata.party.LegalEntity
(name + entity identifier) with the LEI carried per
Party.partyId
typed by
PartyIdentifierTypeEnum
(vocabulary, from the cdm corpus). The house term "counterparty" means this entity; CDM's
Counterparty

type means the role on a trade — not modelled here. Uniqueness and format of the LEI are table rules the platform enforces and tests; an LEI belongs to one entity permanently, so retirement does not free it for re-use.

Rules the table cannot carry: R2 (retirement excludes the entity from the register's selection surface), P3 (retired rows immutable except status/retiredOn), P4 (retirement is one-way — no transition out of retired).
User interface

The bean's search screen and edit form. Retired rows are rendered muted in the default listing, so a user booking a trade does not pick one by mistake — R2 keeps them out of the selection surface regardless.
Dependencies
cdm.base.staticdata.party.LegalEntity
and
cdm.base.staticdata.party.Party
(vocabulary, from the cdm corpus) — the CDM types this bean realises; no CDM table is served on this platform.
FCY standing rule R7 (from the company corpus, standing-rules) — LEI in
partyId
, no free-text counterparty names.
No existing platform entity or registered spec covers this ground (reuse gate: entity catalog and spec registry checked — see property metadata).
Constraints
Volume: ~40 active counterparties plus retired history; no performance target beyond the platform's defaults.
Authorization: any signed-in user may read and maintain the register (platform default).
Considered, none apply: performance target, availability, audit (platform audit trail is automatic), privacy, locale, cost.
Acceptance criteria
A1: retired — covered by the platform's generated test for unique-when-present on LegalEntity.lei.
A2 (verifies R2): WHEN a legal entity is retired, it no longer appears in the register's selection surface, and existing records referencing it remain intact.
A3: retired — covered by the platform's generated test for the table rule format(20 alphanumeric) on LegalEntity.lei.
A4 (verifies P3): WHEN a retired legal entity is edited on any field other than status or retiredOn, the edit is rejected.
A5 (verifies P4): WHEN an edit sets a retired legal entity's status back to draft or active, the edit is rejected.
Migration & compatibility

None — new entity, nothing to migrate. Existing counterparties would be loaded as an initial data load, not a schema migration; whether that load happens and from where is a feature decision, not a spec requirement.
Artifacts
A LegalEntity entity with its observer sheet, default listing and default edit form — the register's screens. No report, import or integration is specified.
Derived from the Data model
Implied by the bean blocks in the Data model and regenerated by the platform - do not edit this block; author above it what the catalog cannot derive.

LegalEntity - persistence.entity (persistence): The entity class with its builder, its descriptor + jsontype entry, its migration and table, and its tests; the descriptor is authored at spec time as the bean's entity-descriptor attachment (entity_descriptors/{qualified-descriptor-name}.json).
LegalEntity - observer.sheet (observer): The observer sheet: the entity's only remote surface, reads and writes.

LegalEntity - ui.defaultForm (ui): The default form of one row, rendered wherever the row is viewed or edited: its layout JS, authored at spec time as the spec's ui/{qualified-descriptor-name}.js attachment and shipped beside the entity class.
LegalEntity.lei - validation.rule (persistence): unique when present - enforced on save and covered by a generated test
LegalEntity.lei - validation.rule (persistence): format(20 alphanumeric) - enforced on save and covered by a generated test
LegalEntity.status - validation.rule (persistence): default(draft) - enforced on save and covered by a generated test
LegalEntity.emirCategory - validation.rule (persistence): default(FC) - enforced on save and covered by a generated test
LegalEntity.segment - validation.rule (persistence): default(INTERDEALER_OTHER) - enforced on save and covered by a generated test
Open Questions
None — the four scope questions were answered in the scoping form (register only; retire-never-delete; LEI optional but unique when present; EMIR category field only).
